data.title: Tencent Expects Lofty AI Spendings to Continue in 2027
data.description:
By Sherry Qin

Tencent executives said the company's elevated artificial-intelligence spending, which has weighed on profit growth, is likely to remain near peak levels next year, while highlighting the revenue potential of its AI agent products.

Tencent has been spending heavily to build AI infrastructure, with cash capital expenditure reaching 65.1 billion yuan in the third quarter. Management said on an earnings call Thursday that AI capital spending will likely remain near current peak levels through the rest of 2026 and into 2027 before easing in 2028.

The outlook comes as investors assess whether China's leading cloud and internet companies are nearing the end of their most aggressive phase of AI investment.

Tencent has lost its position as China's most valuable company by market capitalization in recent months amid investor concerns over whether AI revenue can eventually offset the costs of building and operating the computing infrastructure needed to support the technology.

Its shares fell 6.2% in early Thursday trading amid broader technology-sector losses in Hong Kong.

Still, expectations for future spending have begun to moderate across the sector as improvements in AI model efficiency allow companies to handle more tasks with the same computing resources. Tencent has highlighted its lower-cost Hy4 Flash model as an example of how AI tasks can be processed more efficiently, reducing the need for additional hardware as usage grows.

The spending outlook also comes amid renewed U.S. efforts to restrict China's access to advanced AI chips.

Management said tighter U.S. restrictions could have a greater impact on training future generations of AI models than on its cloud services, which mainly run existing models to generate responses, a process known as inference.

"We're now at a stage where that inference can be run very effectively on a surprisingly limited number of domestic chips," Chief Strategy Officer James Mitchell said.

Executives also highlighted the growing popularity of Tencent's AI workplace assistant WorkBuddy and the revenue potential of Xiaowei, an AI agent integrated into its Weixin messaging app, which is currently under beta testing.

Workbuddy has surpassed 10 million daily active users, with revenue growing more than fivefold from the previous quarter and annualized gross revenue exceeding $500 million over the past week.

Unlike consumer-facing chatbots that have struggled to convert usage into profits, WorkBuddy is designed to perform tasks such as document preparation, data analysis. Tencent President Martin Lau said 60% of China's top 100 companies have already become customers.

Tencent showcased the AI office assistant at this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen, demonstrating how it can help journalists research, write and edit stories, and even order ice cream at the venue.

The focus on WorkBuddy reflects a broader shift in investor attention from AI model capabilities to financial returns.

Management believes Xiaowei could bring AI services to a broad audience by tapping Weixin's 1.44 billion users. With Weixin already generating hundreds of billions of yuan in annual revenue, the AI agent could potentially boost that figure by another 10%-20%, Lau said.

That "will make Xiaowei hugely profitable for us," Lau said, adding that its revenue potential should become clearer over the next six to 12 months.

"Management's candid tone on earnings call should help address investor concerns on chip restriction and future monetization potential for WorkBuddy and Weixin Xiaowei," Citi analysts said in a note.

Write to Sherry Qin at sherry.qin@wsj.com

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Vows to Keep Careful Eye on Fed Moves — Update
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda pledged to closely watch how Federal Reserve policy changes affect growth and inflation in Japan, while reaffirming his readiness to keep tightening monetary settings.

"With the Fed raising interest rates and many other central banks pivoting toward hikes, we need to carefully monitor how those rate moves and the accompanying changes in global financial conditions affect Japan's economy and prices," Ueda told a parliamentary committee on Thursday.

Ueda noted that currency fluctuations--which can be heavily swayed by Fed policy--are more likely to affect domestic prices than in the past as companies in Japan become more comfortable passing on costs to consumers.

"We will conduct monetary policy appropriately while keeping in mind that these shifts could in turn influence underlying inflation through changes in inflation expectations," he added.

While BOJ policymakers are cautious about cooling the economy with monetary tightening, further action looks necessary to keep inflation in check, especially as heightened expectations for Fed rate hikes pressure the yen.

Market participants see a growing chance that the BOJ could raise rates again as soon as December. The Fed is also widely expected to hike next month as U.S. inflation continues to concern officials.

The BOJ is keeping an eye on inflation too. Ueda again stressed the importance of anchoring underlying consumer inflation around 2% so it doesn't overshoot the central bank's target and hurt the economy.

He warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and yen weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October figures due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013. It held policy settings steady at its previous meeting in October after raising rates to 1.25% in September.

Despite the rate hikes delivered so far, the BOJ governor still sees Japan's financial conditions as accommodative, although he acknowledged that monetary tightening is affecting households and businesses through higher mortgage rates and funding costs.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

data.title: MCX share price target raised by UBS backing strong volume growth
data.description:
Shares of Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX) Ltd. declined on Thursday, November 19, even as global investment banking firm UBS reiterated its positive stance and raised its target price on the stock by 18%.

UBS has a "buy" recommendation on MCX and has raised its target price to ₹4,500 from the previous ₹3,800 apiece. This indicates an upside of 24.3% from its previous closing price.

UBS said MCX has improving volume resilience and the potential for its trading activity to sustain at a higher base. Since then, the trading activity has strengthened further in the third quarter of this fiscal, reinforcing the view that the exchange is operating at a structurally-higher activity base, it said.

MCX's average daily transaction free revenue has reached ₹12,700 crore in the third quarter, so far compared to ₹10,900 crore in the previous quarter, with the November month-to-date (MTD) has reached ₹14,300 crore.

At the current volume run rate, the annualized earnings per share (EPS) would be ₹10,000 crore, 15% above the estimated FY28 EPS of ₹87, suggesting further upside, UBS said.

It added that participation has also broadened significantly, with F&O traded clients nearly doubling to 1.5 million in the second quarter from the previous year.

As a result, UBS has raised its EPS estimates for MCX by 4%, 8% and 13% for financial year 2027, 2028 and 2029 respectively.

Of the 17 analysts who have coverage on the stock, 16 have a "buy" rating and one has a "hold" recommendation. The consensus estimates of price targets implies an upside potential of 8.6% from current levels.

Shares of MCX are trading 2.2% lower on Thursday, at ₹3,540.6. The stock is still up 11% over the last one month, taking its year-to-date advance to 62%.

data.title: Fairfax likely buyer in IIFL Capital's $165 million block deal, CNBC-TV18 reports
data.description:
Shares worth 15.40 billion rupees ($164.8 million) in India's IIFL Capital changed hands in a block deal on Thursday, according to exchange data.

Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings was the likely buyer, CNBC-TV18 reported, citing sources.

IIFL Capital and Fairfax did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.

The transaction comes a day after Fairfax sold its entire stake in IIFL Finance , a move Reuters had reported was aimed at unlocking funds for its acquisition of a 60% stake in IDBI Bank from the Indian government and state-owned insurer Life Insurance Corp of India.

The IDBI Bank deal, valued at 528.78 billion rupees ($5.66 billion), ranks among the largest cross-border transactions in India's banking sector.

Fairfax currently owns 38.05% of IIFL Capital Services, which operates investment banking and wealth management businesses, and has previously said it intends to raise its stake to 51%.

The Canadian investor also owns 49% of insurer Digit and plans to consolidate its Indian investments across insurance, investment banking and wealth management under IDBI Bank, creating a diversified financial services group.

($1 = 93.4700 Indian rupees)

data.title: Anthropic, Nvidia And The Next AI Trade: Michael Burry Explains What Could Break The Bull Case
data.description:
Key points:
  • Burry said he may let AI stocks run before shorting them, citing bear market rallies that averaged 22% in the 1930s and 2000s.
  • He sees a threat to Anthropic and Nvidia as businesses build smaller AI models that run on their own machines.
  • Tencent’s 69.1 billion yuan cash burn kept Burry from adding shares. He also thinks private credit buyers may be early.

As Anthropic prepares to go public, “The Big Short” investor Michael Burry sees a rally he might eventually short and also detailed in Nvidia’s earnings he couldn’t overlook: the chipmaker was waiting longer to get paid.

“It is pumping futures for now,” Burry said in his Substack chat when a reader asked about the IPO. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 apiece, above its proposed $70 to $78 range, ahead of Thursday’s expected Nasdaq debut under the ticker ANT.

Burry had already said he would pass on the offering and on buying shares afterward. He put Anthropic’s commitments at more than $1 trillion and questioned whether revenue could grow fast enough to cover them.

Why Burry Might Let AI Stocks Run

When asked whether to buy AI stocks through year-end or sell into a rebound, Burry said he was willing to wait for a better entry on the bearish side. “I cannot give advice but I will look to short on any rip, though I may let it run for a bit; the average bear market rally in both the 1930s and the 2000s was 22%,” he said.

He had made a similar trade last week, doubling his Nasdaq-100 put position when the index bounced from around 27,000. He also bought back some puts on the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) after trimming the bet.

The 4 Extra Days That Caught Burry’s Eye At NVDA

Burry went into Nvidia’s (NVDA) earnings holding $140 puts expiring in February 2027 and passed on buying short-dated calls to cushion the bet. After the results, he said he planned to spend less time covering Nvidia, but one number stood out.

Days sales outstanding, a measure of how long it takes to collect payment, rose to 64 days from 60. Customers owed Nvidia $81 billion at quarter-end, as quarterly revenue more than doubled from a year earlier to $115.8 billion.

“Without Jensen there I wonder how this improves - customers will find it harder to pay, or will just take more time to pay, I imagine,” Burry said, referring to former CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia attributed the increase to the timing of Rubin chip shipments and longer payment terms for some investment-grade customers.

Burry also flagged the wait for Nvidia’s 10-Q, which interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said would arrive in the coming weeks. When a reader questioned why the earnings call lasted just 48 minutes including Q&A, Burry replied, “Earnings calls are controlled environments, and with over 70 sell side analysts covering it, clearly this was invitation only with some instruction.”

When asked how much weight to give the SEC investigation into Nvidia, Burry said, “The SEC just doesn't have the resources or ability to do much.”

Burry Sees A Threat To Anthropic And Nvidia 

A reader who identified themselves as a law firm owner challenged Burry to give an AI agent five years of company filings and ask it to flag changes in depreciation assumptions, down to the exact footnotes.

“As a business owner, I know what an afternoon of my team’s time is worth. Give me that afternoon back every week and I’ll gladly write that check every month,” the reader said.

Burry agreed that kind of tool was coming. He said that businesses could run smaller models on their own machines, using their own records. He said rising costs in China showed how expensive inference (the work a model does to answer a question) could become in the U.S. He also pointed to compression as a way to fit models onto smaller devices.

“I know of people creating their own SLMs inside their homes with AI servers in house. This works against the Anthropic model and the Nvidia model. Brute force and mass resource usage is not the way forward,” he said, referring to small language models.

Nvidia already makes hardware for the market. Its Nemotron 3.5 Bolt model can run on GeForce RTX graphics cards.

Tencent’s Cash Burn Gives Burry A Reason To Wait

Meanwhile, Tencent accounted for just over 2% of Burry’s portfolio earlier this month. The company subsequently reported negative quarterly free cash flow of 69.1 billion yuan.

“It is concerning and the main reason I have not added. I am not sure, if AI bulls are correct, when the hyperscaler spending actually stops or is reduced,” Burry said, referring to spending by the biggest cloud computing companies.

He also questioned whether bargain hunters in private credit were moving too soon. “I've heard capital is already being mobilized to pick at depressed private credit. Could be a self-fulfilling prophecy, but if the size of the AI boom's bust is large enough at the data center level, moves today would likely be overwhelmed and proven early,” he said.

Why Burry Cut His NFLX Target And Stuck With ERO

Burry also explained why his buy target for Netflix (NFLX) had fallen to the high $30s. In July, he had put the low $50s just outside his buying range and questioned the staying power of its hits. “Disney produces wine. Netflix produces milk,” he said at the time.

In the latest chat, Burry said streaming rivals had caught up. “The process of producing hit shows has been a fraught exercise for a long time, and reality TV is a sign of rot in that creative process. It is the cheap more certain option, but one that does not breed network loyalty,” he said.

Burry was equally open about Ero Copper (ERO). In September, he saw a mismatch that favored the miner. Data centers could lift copper demand within two or three years, while new deposits could take about 18 years to reach production.

“My investment in ERO was ill-timed. I still own it in small size but have not added but once,” he said in the latest chat. “I will continue to evaluate it but I think this one has more to it than the AI trade. As I said it is not often I get bullish on a miner.”

data.title: Automakers seek EV-like credits for plug-in hybrids to ease tougher emission norms
data.description:
Automakers are preparing to seek the same regulatory benefits for plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) as fully electric vehicles (EVs) under the upcoming Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFÉ)-III norms, a move that could help manufacturers with large petrol and diesel SUV portfolios meet tighter fleet-level fuel-efficiency requirements.

JSW MG Motor, which has introduced a locally manufactured plug-in hybrid, could be among the immediate beneficiaries. BYD and Stellantis, which are evaluating or planning plug-in hybrid models for India, could also gain if their proposed products reach the market.

The CAFÉ-III norms will come into effect on April 1, 2027, and remain applicable until March 31, 2032. Under the proposed framework, EVs and range-extender electric vehicles (REEVs) receive the highest super-credit multiplier of 3, compared with 2.5 for PHEVs and 1.6 for strong hybrids.

Automakers want PHEVs placed in the same regulatory category as EVs and REEVs, arguing that plug-in hybrids can operate entirely on electric power for shorter journeys despite also having an internal combustion engine.

“In some large auto markets of the world, PHEV is viewed as EV since it can run purely on electric propulsion just like an EV. That is why we are hoping that PHEVs can be seen in the same bracket as EV and REEV,” a senior official at a passenger vehicle manufacturer told Moneycontrol, requesting anonymity as the discussions are still private.

The official said the industry has not yet approached the government but plans to submit its proposal soon.

Who could benefit?

JSW MG Motor is among the clearest potential beneficiaries, having introduced the seven-seater Hector Tomahawk in August 2026, making it the first locally manufactured PHEV in India's mass-market passenger vehicle segment.

The company has already sought more favourable taxation for plug-in hybrids. In August, JSW MG Motor director Parth Jindal said the 40 percent GST rate constrained the company's ability to price the technology competitively.

The Hector Tomahawk PHEV was priced at Rs 25.69 lakh, compared with Rs 19.49 lakh for its electric counterpart, highlighting the pricing challenge facing the technology.

BYD could also benefit as it evaluates plug-in hybrids for India. The Chinese automaker, which has an extensive international PHEV portfolio, has conducted local testing but has yet to finalise the models or their launch timeline.

Stellantis, which operates the Jeep and Citroën brands in India, has included PHEVs in its future product strategy. In October, the company outlined plans for 12 products and upgrades over three years, including vehicles using hybrid, plug-in hybrid and electric powertrains.

Luxury automakers such as Mercedes-Benz and BMW, which already sell plug-in hybrids in India, could also benefit from a higher multiplier, although the impact would depend on their sales volumes and overall fleet composition.

Maruti Suzuki and Toyota, which have invested heavily in hybrid technology, could be potential beneficiaries if they introduce qualifying PHEVs. Their existing strong-hybrid models fall in a separate regulatory category and would not automatically qualify for the proposed higher PHEV credits.

Similarly, manufacturers with large petrol and diesel SUV portfolios, including Mahindra and Tata Motors, could benefit from greater regulatory flexibility if they add PHEVs to their product line-ups. Their existing fully electric models already qualify for the highest multiplier.

There is, however, no confirmation that these manufacturers are individually backing the proposed change. Their potential benefits are based on their existing products, announced strategies and fleet composition.

Compliance challenge

Super credits are important because CAFÉ norms assess a manufacturer's sales-weighted fleet average rather than the emissions or fuel consumption of individual models.

Under the proposed framework, higher multipliers allow qualifying lower-emission vehicles to carry greater weight in compliance calculations, helping manufacturers offset the impact of conventional petrol and diesel models.

This is particularly relevant for automakers with significant SUV sales, since larger and heavier vehicles generally consume more fuel and make fleet-level targets harder to achieve.

Raising the PHEV multiplier from 2.5 to 3 would increase the regulatory benefit of selling such vehicles. The actual advantage would depend on PHEV sales volumes, their certified fuel consumption and the composition of each manufacturer's overall portfolio.

Automakers are also looking at international regulatory practices to support their case.

China classifies EVs, REEVs and PHEVs within its broader new energy vehicle category. In the United States, PHEVs receive partial zero-emission vehicle credits based on their electric driving capability, while range-extender vehicles are generally treated within the PHEV framework.

However, the regulatory treatment of these technologies differs across markets, and their inclusion in a common category does not necessarily mean they receive identical compliance benefits.

India has 13 PHEVs on sale, according to industry estimates cited in the original reporting, but only one is in the non-luxury segment. The remaining models are offered by premium and luxury manufacturers, including Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Ferrari and Lamborghini.

PHEVs combine an internal combustion engine with a rechargeable battery that can be charged externally, much like an EV.

While pure EVs typically offer more than 300 km of electric driving range, PHEVs generally provide around 80–120 km of electric-only driving before relying on their combustion engines for longer journeys. Their batteries can also recover energy through regenerative braking.

The technology therefore offers a middle ground between conventional hybrids and fully electric vehicles, although its real-world fuel consumption and emissions depend significantly on how frequently the battery is charged and how the vehicle is driven.

Taxation is another challenge.

EVs and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles attract GST of 5 percent, while other vehicle technologies are subject to higher rates of 18 percent or 40 percent, depending on classification. Strong hybrids, including the Maruti Suzuki Grand Vitara, Toyota Innova Hycross and Toyota Urban Cruiser Hyryder, fall under the 40 percent bracket.

A higher CAFÉ-III multiplier would not change the GST treatment of PHEVs but could provide manufacturers with an additional incentive to introduce them.

For automakers, the proposed change could offer a way to balance continued demand for petrol and diesel SUVs with increasingly stringent fuel-efficiency requirements. Whether the government accepts the industry's argument will determine how much regulatory support plug-in hybrids receive under India's next phase of emission-related standards.

data.title: Malaysia Consumer Inflation Quickened Slightly in October
data.description:
By Ying Xian Wong

KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia--Malaysia's consumer-price growth in October picked up slightly, mainly driven by higher transport prices.

The consumer-price index for October rose 1.9% compared with the same period a year earlier, the Department of Statistics said Thursday. That compared with September's 1.8% increase and the median forecast for a 2.0% rise from a Wall Street Journal poll of seven economists.

The data follow Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to hold interest rates steady in early November. With analysts seeing scope for a rate increase next year, the outlook for inflation will help shape expectations for the timing of any policy adjustment.

Inflation through the rest of 2026 and into 2027 will continue to be shaped by global commodity and food prices as well as domestic policy changes, RHB senior economist Chin Yee Sian said in a recent note.

Persistent geopolitical uncertainties and prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have heightened the risk of further increases in crude oil prices.

However, price controls, subsidies and a relatively stable ringgit are expected to temper how much higher costs will be passed through to consumers, keeping both headline and core inflation manageable, she added.

The figures offer a gauge of how those competing forces are affecting household costs. Prices for food and nonalcoholic beverages, which together account for nearly 30% of the CPI basket, rose 1.7% from a year earlier in October.

Core inflation, which excludes volatile fresh-food prices and government-administered items, was 1.5%, compared with 1.7% in September.

On a monthly basis, consumer prices rose 0.1% in October, unchanged from the previous month.

data.title: Chrysos Corporation Lifts Revenue 27% on Record Gold Assay Volumes
data.description:
Chrysos Corporation has lifted unaudited revenue 27% to $36.7 million in the first four months of the 2027 financial year as demand for its PhotonAssay gold-testing technology continues to grow.

Its global fleet analysed 4.91 million samples between July and October, a 43% increase on the corresponding period, while October brought a new monthly record of 1.36 million samples.

After signing 15 new lease agreements this financial year, Chrysos has 97 PhotonAssay units under contract and has reaffirmed its full-year revenue and earnings forecasts.

Chrysos has also lifted its manufacturing capacity to 18 units annually as it works towards a target of 90 deployed systems by the end of the 2029 financial year.

Growing AAC Returns

Minimum monthly assay payments contributed $22.6m, up 7%, while additional assay charges (AAC) jumped 79% to $13.7m as customers processed more samples through existing machines.

Usage-based AAC now represents 38% of PhotonAssay revenue compared with 26% a year earlier, reflecting an increasing contribution from work performed above contracted minimum volumes.

Sample processing has exceeded one million a month since March, with October throughput alone running 48% ahead of the same month last year.

“We’ve built a business model that works throughout the mining cycle—minimum monthly payments give us a secure base and, when activity is high, additional assay charges let us share in the upside,” managing director Dirk Treasure said.

“Just as importantly, the fleet, has on average sustained above 90% availability from July to October, despite many units running at very high utilisation.”

New Global Contracts

Eleven of the 15 lease agreements were signed after the company’s August results, including two directly with miners and nine through laboratory partners.

The growing order book sits alongside six systems deployed since the start of the financial year, bringing the operational PhotonAssay fleet to 51 units across five continents after a decommissioning in Mali.

New installations span Australia, Canada, Suriname, and Ivory Coast, taking the technology into both established mining centres and newer markets.

Another six units are being deployed, while four are awaiting installation and four remain in storage or are being prepared for shipment.

Full-Year Outlook Remains Unchanged

For the 2027 financial year, revenue guidance remains at $108m to $118m and EBITDA are forecast at $35m to $42m on a constant-currency basis.

The company held $19.5m in cash at 31 October and had $120m undrawn under its $200m syndicated debt facility.

That gives it a robust funding position to support the manufacture and installation of the growing number of contracted machines.

For Chrysos, the immediate task is to convert its contracted pipeline into working systems while maintaining the sample volumes that have fuelled the early-year revenue growth.

data.title: China's yuan steady as Trump-Xi meeting in focus
data.description:
China's yuan was steady on Thursday despite dollar strength as investors focused on talks between Chinese and US leaders in China's tech hub Shenzhen.

Chinese President Xi Jinping called for open cooperation at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, ahead of a historic meeting with US President Donald Trump and Russian leader Vladimir Putin.

The talks between China and the US will likely focus on topics including tariffs, trade, rare-earth and chip export controls, Nanhua Futures said in a note to clients.

"If the talks yield little beyond rhetoric, the impact on the yuan and Chinese stocks would be limited," the brokerage said.

"However, an extension of the trade truce or an easing of restrictions on rare earths and semiconductors could give a boost to yuan assets."

China's onshore yuan was little changed in morning trading, changing hands at around 6.6667 per dollar.

The currency has rallied nearly 5% so far this year, despite a bullish dollar.

The dollar index on Thursday rose to the highest since April 2025 and is set for an eight-session rising streak as traders strengthened bets on US rate hikes.

The Federal Reserve's meeting minutes showed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation.

On Thursday, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva called for a tightening of monetary policy in many economies to fight inflation.

data.title: JOYY Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: Total revenues record consistent increases, driven by sustained growth of three core businesses
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- JOYY Inc. () ("JOYY" or the "Company"), a leading global technology company, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

In the third quarter, JOYY maintained solid growth momentum. Total revenues reached US$624.6 million, up 15.6% year over year and 5.7% quarter over quarter. Social entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, up 8.8% year over year. BIGO Ads, including both first-party and third-party businesses, generated US$145.7 million in revenue, up 39.6% year over year, with its third-party advertising business sustaining strong growth of 52.3% year over year. SHOPLINE revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year. The contribution from non-livestreaming revenue further increased to 32.8% of total revenues this quarter, driven by the Company's multi-engine growth strategy.

JOYY's non-GAAP operating income reached US$46.6 million, up 14.6% year over year. Non-GAAP EBITDA reached US$55.7 million, up 10.1% year over year. Operating cash inflow for the quarter was US$102.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, JOYY held US$2.94 billion in net cash. Supported by the Company's strong cash flow generation and solid financial position, it continued to return capital to its shareholders for their long-term support through cash dividends and share repurchases. As of November 13, the Company has returned a total of US$536.0 million to shareholders this year.

Ms. Ting Li, Chairperson and Chief Executive Officer of JOYY, commented, "We have continued to execute our multi-engine growth strategy, strengthening our core Social Entertainment business while developing Ad Tech and Smart Commerce as two new growth engines. Following our investments and business model validation over the past few years, the results of this strategy are becoming increasingly evident in sustained topline expansion. Looking ahead to 2027, we believe JOYY will enter an important phase as we advance our multi-engine growth strategy and translate our progress into stronger operating results. With increasingly clear growth paths across our three businesses, we are confident in the Company's ability to sustain solid revenue growth in 2027. We also expect greater scale, a stronger earnings mix, and improved operating efficiency to drive further growth in operating profitability."

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were US$624.6 million, representing an increase of 15.6% from US$540.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 5.7% from US$590.8 million in the second quarter of 2026.- Social Entertainment revenue was US$441.0 million, representing an increase of 8.8% from US$405.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 4.3% from US$422.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.- BIGO Ads revenue was US$145.7 million, representing an increase of 39.6% from US$104.4 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 9.0% from US$133.7 million in the second quarter of 2026.- SHOPLINE revenue was US$37.8 million, representing an increase of 24.7% from US$30.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase of 10.0% from US$34.4 million in the second quarter of 2026.
  • Operating income was US$13.5 million.
  • Non-GAAP1 operating income was US$46.6 million, representing an increase of 14.6% from US$40.7 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Non-GAAP1 EBITDA was US$55.7 million, representing an increase of 10.1% from US$50.6 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Net cash as of September 30, 2026 was US$2940.5 million.
  • Net cash from operating activities was US$102.2 million.

Third Quarter 2026 Business Highlights

Social Entertainment Business

In the third quarter, Social Entertainment continued to deliver steady growth, with year-over-year growth momentum further accelerating. The Company's global average mobile MAUs reached 278.8 million, up 4.7% year over year. Livestreaming revenue reached US$419.8 million, up 8.1% year over year and 4.3% quarter over quarter. Driven by effective and refined operations, the number of core livestreaming paying users grew 8.1% year over year and 4.8% quarter over quarter.

Bigo Live, the Company's flagship product, continued its steady revenue growth, supported by ongoing improvements in content operations, its streamer ecosystem, and AI applications. In content operations, Bigo Live continued to build on its strengths as a global social platform to better cater to users' cross-regional content consumption and social interaction needs. Bigo Live further refined its cross-regional content distribution algorithms, expanded live translation coverage, and enhanced speech recognition in complex acoustic environments, making it easier for cross-language communication. These improvements drove continued growth in cross-regional gifting among users in developed markets. In terms of the streamer ecosystem, Bigo Live continued to invest in its community by refining growth and incentive mechanisms for new streamers. In particular, Bigo Live improved onboarding and guidance to help newly signed streamers successfully launch their first livestreams. These efforts contributed to a 4.7-percentage-point increase in the share of newly signed streamers completing their first livestream compared with the previous quarter, bolstering Bigo Live's high-quality content pipeline. Bigo Live continued to integrate AI into livestream interactions and virtual gifting, expanding its AI-generated interactive content and virtual gifts to create a more personalized experience for users. In September, the share of total virtual gift consumption attributable to AI-generated interactive virtual gifts increased further to 35.4%.

Furthermore, Bigo Live continued to deepen local community engagement and foster vibrant creator ecosystems. In the Middle East and North Africa, as an official content partner of the 2026 Esports World Cup, Bigo Live delivered an immersive viewing format that integrated tournament livestreams with interactive experiences. Across Southeast Asia, Bigo Live hosted multiple mid-year galas in local markets, supporting the growth of local creators and the sustainable development of its ecosystem. In North America, BIGO Academy combined online growth challenges with offline recognition, highlighting the vitality of its creator ecosystem and strong user engagement. In South America, Bigo Live held its inaugural offline event in Brazil and organized roadshows in Colombia and Peru, expanding public awareness of the platform and fostering a more vibrant and inclusive local creator ecosystem.

BIGO Ads Advertising Technology Business

In the third quarter, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global traffic network, diversify its advertiser verticals and demand mix, while improving its algorithms and ad delivery efficiency. As a result, BIGO Ads' revenue reached US$145.7 million, up 39.6% year over year and 9.0% quarter over quarter. Its third-party advertising business, BIGO Audience Network, grew 52.3% year over year and 9.2% quarter over quarter.

On the supply side, BIGO Ads continued to expand its global developer ecosystem and broaden the high-quality traffic coverage. In the third quarter, SDK traffic grew 55.6% year over year. In October, BIGO Ads SDK became generally available via Google AdMob™ Mediation as an in-app bidding partner. Developers can now seamlessly access the BIGO Ads SDK through Google AdMob Mediation and tap into massive demand from global premium advertisers. This integration creates new opportunities for BIGO Ads to expand its premium traffic supply and reach a broader range of app categories.

On the demand side, BIGO Ads continued to strengthen its presence in key verticals by expanding its local advertiser base and accumulating more advertiser conversion data. These insights helped further refine its algorithms and optimize ad delivery solutions across different web-based verticals. Web-based advertising demand continued to accelerate, growing by approximately 328% year over year and 30% quarter over quarter, becoming a key driver of BIGO Ads' growth this quarter. Meanwhile, in-app demand maintained healthy growth momentum.

On the technology side, BIGO Ads continued to enhance its data and AI-driven algorithm capabilities to improve the precision and efficiency of ad delivery. As its cross-channel attribution systems improved and advertiser conversion data accumulated, the platform further upgraded its model architecture to support multiple conversion objectives and types of traffic, improving algorithm accuracy and iteration efficiency. Meanwhile, BIGO Ads continued to refine its bidding strategies to better assess the value of each ad impression and match advertiser budgets with available inventory more effectively. These improvements helped advertisers meet their ROI targets while enhancing the efficiency of BIGO Ads' traffic acquisition and monetization.

SHOPLINE E-Commerce Business

In the third quarter, SHOPLINE continued to focus on acquiring high-quality brand merchants, strengthening its presence in key markets, and enhancing its omnichannel commerce infrastructure and value-added services. SHOPLINE's revenue reached US$37.8 million, up 24.7% year over year and 10.0% quarter over quarter.

In the cross-border business, SHOPLINE enhanced its service offerings and local support to help these merchants migrate to its platform, manage operations across markets, and process cross-border transactions more efficiently. In the third quarter, revenue from cross-border merchants maintained strong momentum, growing 77.8% year over year. To support the growing base of brand merchants, the Company continued to enhance SHOPLINE Payments with more local payment options, stronger multi-currency payment support, and improved transaction management. These enhancements helped merchants manage cross-border payments easily and efficiently.

In AI Commerce, SHOPLINE's strategy revolves around helping merchants capture demand from AI channels and improve their operational efficiency. As AI agents change how consumers discover and purchase products, SHOPLINE continued to strengthen its capabilities and expand integrations with the broader AI ecosystem. While volume from AI channels is still in an early stage, adoption is building quickly. In the third quarter, page views and order volume from AI channels grew nearly 500% and 550% year over year, respectively. Notably, AI is demonstrating distinct advantages in categories such as consumer electronics and furniture, where shoppers weigh multiple options before buying. In these categories, AI can better interpret consumer needs, recommend relevant products, and guide shoppers toward a purchase. SHOPLINE Omi, an AI-powered commerce assistant, has rolled out features spanning product management, customer segmentation, promotional events, guidance on platform features and settings, and detailed store performance analysis, bringing AI deeper into merchants' day-to-day workflows and improving operational efficiency.

data.title: IIFL Capital shares worth ₹1,505 crore change hands in a block deal; Promoters likely sellers
data.description:
A large trade took place in IIFL Capital Ltd., during the pre-open block deal window on Thursday, November 19, where sources tell CNBC-TV18 that promoters of the company are likely to have sold stake.

As many as 4.4 crore shares or, 11.8% of the company's equity changed hands in the block deal, as per the data available.

Shares changed hands at an average price of ₹350 per share, taking the total transaction value to ₹1,505 crore.

While buyers and sellers are not officially known, sources told CNBC-TV18 that promoters Nirmal Jain and R Venkataraman are likely to be the sellers in this transaction.

Sources also said that Fairfax is the likely buyer in this transaction, where promoters are likely to have sold stake, and is likely to be a part of the deal between the two entities.

In case Fairfax is indeed the buyer in the transaction, it will increase its holding in IIFL Capital to 51%. Currently, FIH Maurutius Investments, the Fairfax entity, held a 38.04% stake in IIFL Capital at the end of the September quarter.

FIH Mauritius exited its entire holding in IIFL Finance via a block deal on Wednesday, with the sale of its remaining 13.25% stake.

SBI MF, HDFC MF, Franklin Templeton MF, Aditya Birla Sun Life MF, Nippon MF, among other marquee funds were buyers in that transaction. Blackstone, Goldman Sachs, Citigroup are among the foreign buyers in the deal, while investors like Rohit Kothari, Madhu Kela, Mukul Agrawal and Akash Bhansali were also among the buyers.

Shares of IIFL Capital Services are trading 2% lower after the block deal on Thursday at ₹346.45. The stock is down 10% so far this year.

data.title: Indian shares off to a muted start as hawkish Fed minutes weigh
data.description:
Indian shares opened little changed on Thursday as a hawkish tone from the US Federal Reserve in its latest policy meeting minutes offset optimism over easing crude oil prices and sustained foreign fund inflows.

The Nifty 50 fell 0.16% to 25,186.80 and the Sensex edged 0.05% higher to 82,074.16, as of 9:15 a.m. IST.

The October minutes of the Fed's meeting showed policymakers saw a need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for now.

Higher US interest rates make the dollar and US Treasuries attractive for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), which could draw capital away from emerging market equities.

Metals fell 1% and IT dropped 0.7%. A firmer dollar makes metals more expensive for buyers with other currencies, while expectations of higher rates fuelled concerns about client spending for IT companies, which earn a significant share of their revenue from the US.

Ten of the 16 major sectors declined at the open. The broader small-caps and mid-caps shed 0.1% and 0.3%, respectively.

($1 = 93.4700 Indian rupees)

data.title: Currency Check | Rupee opens flat at 93.44 against dollar; Asian peers trade mixed
data.description:
The Indian rupee opened flat on November 19, with sustained foreign equity inflows cushioning it against dollar strength amid hawkish Federal Reserve signals.

The rupee opened flat at 93.44 per dollar, compared with previous close of 93.44.

According to Finrex, Indian Rupee Is set to open flat today as we await for inflows from the Mahanadi Coal fields IPO which is open for Retail and HNI today. Outflows in the form and NDF expiry are also expected today.

The narrow range of 93.25 to 93.75 is expected by the market today with initially selling of the inflows while later the buying of $ happening to square up the NDF position.

Exporters should take advantage of the upside and sell their export receivables for near term while importers to continue buying dollar to hedge their payables in the near term, it added.

Asian currencies traded on a mixed note against the US dollar, with the Malaysian ringgit emerging as the top gainer, rising 0.21 percent, followed by the Indonesian rupiah, which strengthened 0.13 percent. The Thai baht gained 0.07 percent, while the Singapore dollar and Philippine peso edged up 0.02 percent and 0.01 percent, respectively.

On the other hand, the Taiwan dollar weakened 0.10 percent, while the South Korean won and Chinese yuan declined 0.04 percent each. The Japanese yen also slipped 0.03 percent against the greenback.

The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Fed official pointed to further interest rate hikes.

The dollar index was roughly flat at 103.81 in early Asia trade, hovering near its highest level since April 2025.

data.title: Fujitsu expands strategic partnership with Google Cloud to accelerate AI transformation
data.description:
KAWASAKI, Japan, Nov 19, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Limited today announced that it has expanded its strategic partnership [1] with Google Cloud to accelerate the secure use of AI and cloud technologies, as well as AI transformation (AX), for both enterprises and society. Fujitsu will combine its long-standing industry and operational expertise, technology, and implementation capabilities with Google Cloud's advanced AI, AI agents, cybersecurity, data analytics, and cloud technologies to support customers' AX and drive the creation and expansion of new businesses.

As part of this expanded partnership, Fujitsu will increase its internal utilization of Google Cloud's AI and cloud technologies to drive its own operational transformation. Furthermore, Fujitsu will leverage the insights and expertise gained through this internal practice as a "customer zero" initiative to provide value to a wide range of customers.

Fujitsu is advancing specific initiatives under this partnership, focusing on cybersecurity, cloud utilization for high-security requirements, the strengthening of Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs), and the promotion of AI in the retail sector. Through this strengthened collaboration, Fujitsu aims to support customers in securely advancing their AX by integrating Google Cloud's advanced technologies with Fujitsu's industry expertise, the enterprise-grade generative AI "Takane," the AI platform "Fujitsu Kozuchi," and Fujitsu's robust implementation capabilities.

Key Initiatives of the Collaboration

1. AI-enhanced cybersecurity:

As cyberattacks become increasingly sophisticated and complex, Fujitsu is participating as a launch partner for Google AI Threat Defense (AITD), which Google Cloud began providing in Japan in July 2026. By combining Google Cloud's extensive security technologies-including Wiz, Mandiant, Google Security Operations, and CodeMender-with Fujitsu's deep expertise in cybersecurity and customer systems, the companies will provide advanced solutions that support a secure AI and cloud environment for customers.

2. Cloud utilization in high-security domains:

Fujitsu aims to deliver the value of cloud and AI even to customers requiring high-level security and data protection. By combining Google Distributed Cloud-a highly secure cloud that can be utilized in on-premises and closed environments-with Fujitsu's expertise and technology in mission-critical areas such as public and social infrastructure, the two companies will explore the secure use of cloud and AI in environments requiring high confidentiality and data sovereignty.

3. Supporting customer transformation with AI-focused FDEs:

Fujitsu is promoting AI implementation through Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs) who work deeply within business frontlines to solve challenges and create new value. To empower FDEs to focus more on customer engagement and value creation, Fujitsu is providing a platform on Google Cloud that streamlines and accelerates AI implementation. By leveraging Google Cloud's AI and AI agent technologies, including Gemini, Fujitsu will enable FDEs to focus on essential problem-solving and maximize the value delivered to customers.

4. Promoting AI in retail:

Fujitsu is accelerating AX in the retail industry by combining its long-standing industry and operational expertise with Google's extensive consumer touchpoints and AI technologies. This initiative aims to advance store operations and create new shopping experiences that connect consumers with products and services through AI. Through Uvance for Retail, Fujitsu aims to provide value with a vision toward the era of agentic commerce [2] .

Takahito Tokita, Representative Director, CEO, Fujitsu Limited, comments:

By bringing together Google Cloud's world-leading AI and cloud technologies and Fujitsu's deep industry expertise and proven ability to implement solutions in mission-critical environments, we will accelerate transformation even for customers with the most demanding security and data protection requirements. Going forward, Fujitsu will actively leverage Google Cloud technologies to advance our own transformation and by applying the insights gained through these efforts for customers across all industries, we will further drive growth for both companies.

Thomas Kurian, CEO, Google Cloud, comments:

By combining Google Cloud's advanced agentic AI and security technologies with Fujitsu's deep mission-critical expertise, we're empowering organizations to drive business transformation with confidence. From strengthening AI-powered cyber defense to pioneering new experiences like agentic commerce, our expanded partnership unlocks transformative value for customers worldwide.

[1] Expanded its strategic partnership:

Fujitsu and Google Cloud Japan G.K. signed an MOU (Memorandum of Understanding) in July 2026 regarding a strategic collaboration for formulating joint solutions and Go-to-Market (GTM) plans, and have now expanded the scope of this partnership.

[2] Agentic Commerce:

An initiative to create new purchasing experiences and retail business models for an era where AI agents that support individual consumers connect with AI agents used in various industries-not only retail but also manufacturing and logistics-to transform the entire process from product discovery, selection, and purchasing to the post-purchase experience.

About Fujitsu

Fujitsu's purpose is to make the world more sustainable by building trust in society through innovation. As the digital transformation partner of choice for customers around the globe, our 100,000 employees work to resolve some of the greatest challenges facing humanity. Our range of services and solutions draw on five key technologies: AI, Computing, Networks, Data & Security, and Converging Technologies, which we bring together to deliver sustainability transformation. Fujitsu Limited (TSE:6702) reported consolidated revenues of 3.5 trillion yen (US$23 billion) for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 and remains the top digital services company in Japan by market share. data.title: India's liquor stocks fall as bulk Scotch imports face higher duties
data.description:
Shares of Indian liquor makers fell between 1.2% and 3.2% on Thursday after Reuters reported that India was imposing a 162.5% duty and tax on bulk Scotch whisky imports, raising concerns over higher costs and potential supply disruptions.

As of 9:16 AM IST, shares of Tilaknagar Industries fell 1.2% to 529.05 rupees, Radico Khaitan dropped 3.18% to 4,516.70 rupees, Allied Blenders and Distillers was down 1.59% at 785.40 rupees and United Spirits fell 1.54% to 1,415.5 rupees.
